lots.guide_summary: All evidence is Gowans SOLD hammer prices in AUD (rate 1.0), no unsold or asking found. Nine plain single tins of world coins sold $35 to $100 hammer in Oct 2025 to Jul 2026, most $45 to $65 (median about $50). Two small tobacco tins went for only $11 and $15 (Dec 2025) and two tins plus notes made $110. Component guides: a single Kennedy half $25, a graded MS67 Ike $28. This lot has more than a typical tin (Barber silver coin, 40% half, Ike, two slabs), so it should sit in the upper half of the tin range, but none of the sold tins are the same contents.
lots.working: Keep: lowest plain single-tin SOLD in the last 24 months = $35 (Apr 2026); $35 / 1.198 = $29.22, round down to $25. The $11 and $15 small tobacco-tin sales are excluded from the keep floor as not comparable in quantity (they hold far fewer coins and no US holders) but are kept as category guides. Flip: likely resale about $50 (median single-tin sale); less about 13% selling fees ($6.50) and about $15 postage for a heavy tin = $28.50; $28.50 / 2.396 = $11.89, round down to $10. Flip margin is thin. Inbound freight $0 (pickup Moonah). Melt floor not computed (silver spot not fetched today: goldprice.org returned Forbidden); silver content is roughly 4.6g fine in a 40% Kennedy plus about 5.6g fine in a Barber quarter (or 11.3g if a half).
lots.confidence_reason: Holder labels read (2015-D Roosevelt 10c BU, 40% Silver Kennedy, Collectors Alliance) and Ike identified by design and size, but the Barber coin date and the rest of the tin cannot be read. Many SOLD tins opened, but they are close rather than the same contents.
lots.condition: Tin worn. Barber coin heavily worn. Ike circulated in a soft flip. Kennedy half lightly toned in a card holder. Slabs look clean.
lots.key_photo_findings: Dollar in flip shows the Apollo 11 eagle-landing-on-moon reverse with ONE DOLLAR and E PLURIBUS UNUM; diameter about 1.16 to 1.25 times the Kennedy half, so a 38mm Eisenhower, not a Peace dollar. Kennedy card reads '40% Silver Kennedy Half Dollar', date 196x. INB label reads '2015-D ROOSEVELT 10c BRILLIANT UNCIRCULATED'. A capsuled coin at top of the tin shows a worn Barber (Liberty head) obverse, likely 90% silver. Several capsuled modern US cents.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped; all 14 researcher entries matched the Gowans API (prices, bid counts and dates confirmed). Added two SOLD entries the researcher left out from the same search: $11 and $15 tobacco tins of world coins (Dec 2025), which drag the low end down. Same_item labels kept as close or category guide.
lots.question_for_gowans: What is the date and denomination of the capsuled Barber coin (quarter or half), and are there any other silver coins in the tin? What is the date on the Kennedy half and the Eisenhower dollar (is the Ike a 40% silver S-mint)? What coin is in the Collectors Alliance slab?

lots.what_it_is: Royal Australian Mint 1988 mint set (Bicentennial outer card with Sydney Cove painting, yellow 'The New Impressions' inner card, 1c to $2) plus a Macquarie Mint folder 'The History of Australians in WWI': 'We Will Remember Them' silver commemorative release (Light Horse), 'Gallipoli Landing' gold commemorative release (gold-coloured), and 8 silver-look capsuled medallions (Simpson and his Donkey, HMAS Sydney, Sir John Monash, Enlist Now, Victoria Cross, Royal Australian Artillery, Battle of Bullecourt, Villers-Bretonneux). Macquarie Mint is a private distributor; these folder pieces are almost certainly plated base-metal medallions, not legal tender or bullion. The Gowans title singles out one 'silver coin'.
